servers.title: Upstreams
servers.desc: Shared upstream library: alias, address, TCP/UDP (empty = off), and enable. Entry type and listen live on Forwards.
servers.add_description: Creates an upstream only — no forwards. Add entries under Forwards, or use Add entry on a row.
servers.name: Name
servers.port_enable_hint: Fill a port to enable that protocol; leave empty to skip.
servers.need_ports: Enter at least one TCP or UDP port
servers.confirm_body: Deletes “%s” and its forwards. Irreversible until you restore from Changes.
servers.empty_hint: Add an upstream, or Quick onboard in batch; then configure entries under Forwards.
servers.promote_hint: Enable production forwards for this upstream; creates them if missing
servers.promote_confirm: Enable production forwards for %s? (Validation stays unchanged; missing forwards are created.)
servers.quick_description: Batch-write upstreams, optionally with first production entries (validation optional). Then Apply config.
servers.quick_done_body: Upstreams written. Checked entries are created too. Review under Apply config.
servers.quick_need_rows: Add at least one valid upstream row
servers.quick_paste_hint: One per line: alias IP:port, e.g. server-01 185.244.208.205:4301
rules.title: Forwards
rules.desc: Entry type, protocol, listen, and toggles. Upstream address/ports come from Upstreams. Rollback = disable production.
rules.empty_hint: Use Add forward to pick an upstream and entry type, or Add entry from Upstreams.
acl.title: Access lists
acl.desc: Maintain allow/deny source IPs (CIDR) that may reach the listen ports.
acl.add_description: Pick a list and enter a CIDR or IP.
acl.empty_hint: Add a CIDR or IP to this list.
config.title: Config
config.desc: Edit the full YAML in place; save replaces the whole file and overwrites unsaved form edits.
config.edit_warning: Save replaces the whole file and overwrites unsaved form edits.
config.saved_hint: Save ≠ push to the data plane. Apply uses hot/hard routing; hard reload drops existing connections. When ready:
config.toast_conflict: File changed elsewhere; reloaded — edit again
apply.title: Apply
apply.desc: Save writes disk only. Two actions: apply locally (this host only) or publish to the fleet (nodes pull and align).
apply.risk_body: Local hot apply: no drain, no Envoy restart. Local hard reload: drain + restart Envoy and drop sessions on this host. Publishing to the fleet never triggers a global hard restart.
apply.publish_confirm_body: Publishes the current intent as a new fleet version; gateway nodes will pull and hot-apply locally. Misaligned nodes can be retried — no automatic global hard restart. Prefer applying locally first.
apply.reload_confirm_body: Backs up, renders, and hard-restarts Envoy on this host. Impact: all existing TCP/UDP sessions on this gateway drop and must reconnect; new traffic may be removed from the load balancer during the drain window.
apply.hot_confirm_body: Backs up and hot-pushes config via the local control plane (no drain, no Envoy restart). Unrelated long connections should survive; flows on changed/removed listeners may drain.
apply.fw_confirm_body: Flushes and loads nftables (may briefly affect host ingress). Mistakes can break SSH — keep this session and have cloud console ready. Does not usually restart Envoy, but bad rules can block ingress traffic.
apply.none_hint: After you save config, pending summaries and results show here.
ops.title: Ops
ops.desc: Local only: diagnostics, drain, smoke/canary, firewall check, and profiles. Fleet publish/join/leave live under Fleet.
fleet.title: Fleet
fleet.desc: Node registry, publish overview, join and leave. Control publishes a version; node agents pull and align.
fleet.empty_hint: Use Join node to issue a bootstrap token, install the node component, and start the agent.
fleet.publish_desc: Current fleet-visible config version; write actions live under Apply → Publish to fleet.
fleet.join_desc: Issue a one-time token and bootstrap hints; install with the node template and run the agent. LB attach stays manual.
fleet.join_confirm_body: Creates node identity and a one-time join credential. Finish install on the target host. LB attach stays manual.
fleet.leave_desc: Remove from the registry and revoke the agent token. LB detach stays manual.
fleet.leave_confirm_body: Removes the node from the registry and revokes its agent credential. LB detach stays manual.
ops.drain_confirm_fail: Posts healthcheck/fail on this Envoy so LB/NLB stop sending new connections (waits DRAIN_WAIT). Established flows usually stay; on a single node this gateway stops accepting new connections.
ops.drain_confirm_ok: Posts healthcheck/ok so LB/NLB resume sending new connections to this node.
ops.drain_hint: Stops new traffic; may wait tens of seconds. Existing connections usually remain — do not drain a lone production node by mistake.
ops.profile_confirm_body: Writes host defaults only; does not restart Envoy yet. You still need Apply config afterward, which will interrupt existing connections.
ops.profile_empty_hint: This host has no ops profiles, or they failed to load.
ops.fw_root_hint:
Firewall ops need the privileged helper. Check:
1) /usr/local/libexec/relaygate/apply is installed
2) /etc/sudoers.d/relaygate-panel allows relaygate NOPASSWD for that helper
3) Panel unit does not set NoNewPrivileges (or options that imply it)
Then: systemctl restart relaygate-panel
ops.profile_applied_body: Defaults written. Apply config; run firewall apply if nftables changed.
changes.title: Changes
changes.desc: Browse change summaries by timestamp and roll back when needed.
changes.empty_hint: Applies leave timestamped summaries you can review or roll back.
changes.rollback_body: Restores that stamp and force-recreates Envoy. Impact: all existing connections on this gateway drop. Use a maintenance window or drain dual-active first.
changes.no_summary: (no summary file; stamp can still be rolled back)
monitoring.use_sidebar: Please open Monitoring from the sidebar (new window).
